disposition_reason: Narrative review of heavy metals in food; cocoa content is limited to secondary table rows quoting other studies: Cd in chocolate, Belgium 0.010-0.090 mg/kg [ref 131, Vromman et al.] and Serbia 0.034 mg/kg [ref 143, Skrbic et al.]; Pb 15.306 ug/kg and Sn 6.01 ug/kg for a mixed Italian category 'sweets, chocolate, cakes (and other pastries)'; and a claimed 'EFSA' Ni maximum level of 0.80 mg/kg for chocolate and cocoa products. No primary measurements, n, method or basis are given for the cocoa rows.
disposition_locator: Table 1 (PDF p.4); Table 3 Cadmium (PDF p.24-25); Table 4 Lead (PDF p.27); Table 6 Tin (PDF p.32)

regulatory.status: claimed by review; not verifiable as an EU maximum level

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary reproduces 'Ni Chocolate and cocoa products 0.80 mg/kg EFSA' as if a regulatory limit; primary attributes it to EFSA but this is not a real EU ML.
unresolved: Ni 0.80 mg/kg 'EFSA' maximum level for chocolate/cocoa does not correspond to any EU regulatory maximum (EFSA does not set MLs; no EU Ni ML exists for cocoa); treat as unreliable and do not use as regulatory value.

Belgian chocolate Cd 0.010-0.090 mg/kg (Vromman et al., ref 131) and Serbian chocolate Cd 0.034 mg/kg (Skrbic et al., ref 143) are secondary restatements; primary papers are not in wiki/sources and were not checked. Not extracted as occurrence rows from this review because n, basis, chocolate type and method are absent.
Italian Pb/Sn rows are for a mixed sweets/chocolate/cakes category, out of cocoa scope.
